A flexible container the team uses to group related user stories. It might follow a column on the story map, a variation such as one document type, or a whole slice. Epics are optional and sit outside the chain: every story links to its Deliverable, and may also belong to an epic. The one rule: an epic stays inside one Solution. Epics live in the backlog, not on the roadmap.

- **Definition:** [Glossary: Epic](/system/glossary)
- **How it works:** [11 Deliverables and user stories](/system/deliverables-and-user-stories)
- **Owner:** product owner, with the development team
- **Links to:** [Solution](/templates/solution) it sits inside; [User story](/templates/user-story) it groups; [Deliverable](/templates/deliverable) its stories belong to, if known

## Template

| Field | What goes here |
| --- | --- |
| Epic | Short name for what groups these stories |
| Solution | The Solution it sits inside |
| Grouped by | Map column, variation, slice or other, so readers know the shape |
| Deliverables | The Deliverables its stories belong to, if known |
| Size | Optional T-shirt size |
| Stories | The stories in it, linked |
| Status | Open or Done. Deliverables carry the commitment status |

## DMV example

| Field | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| Epic | Birth certificate check |
| Solution | License Ready Check |
| Grouped by | Variation: one document type |
| Deliverables | Pre-check for birth certificates and proof of address (Q3) |
| Size | S |
| Stories | Submit a birth certificate photo. Review a birth certificate. Know the review result. Clerk sees the result at the counter. |
| Status | Open |

The team grouped this Deliverable's stories by document type, so it has a second epic, Proof of address check. Another team might have grouped License Ready Check by map column instead, with an epic such as "Check documents before the visit" running across the Q3, Q4 and Q1 Deliverables. Both work.
